title: First hour of an acute asthma attack in a 7-year-old
alt: Assess, give oxygen, grade the attack, treat by severity, give prednisolone and reassess.
caption: Doses after BTS/SIGN 2019 and GINA 2024 acute asthma guidance.

nodes.text: 7-year-old in acute asthma attack: ABCDE, sit upright, call for senior help
Oxygen by mask to keep SpO2 94-98%
Assess severity: SpO2, speech, PEF, HR, RR, consciousness, work of breathing
Silent chest, exhaustion, cyanosis or drowsiness?
Life-threatening: ICU and anaesthetist, continuous salbutamol plus ipratropium, IV magnesium
Severe? SpO2 under 92%, cannot complete sentences, PEF under 50%
Severe: nebulised salbutamol 2.5-5 mg plus ipratropium 0.5 mg, repeat every 20 min
Mild-moderate: salbutamol 2-10 puffs via spacer, repeat every 20 min
One puff at a time, 5 breaths each; nebulise if too breathless
Prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg by mouth (max 40 mg) within the first hour
Salbutamol every 20-30 min, spacing out as PEF rises
Repeat salbutamol with ipratropium, IV magnesium 40-50 mg/kg over 20 min, senior review
Admit or observe; steroid for 3-5 days; discharge when PEF over 75% predicted
